# Breast Cancer Spatial Transcriptomics

## Library loading

```{r}
library(BayesSpace)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(ggspavis)
library(scater)
library(scran)
library(scrapper)
library(SpatialExperiment)
```

## Data loading

```{r}
spe <- load('Breast_ST5.RData')
```

## Preliminary data exploration

Number of genes and rows

```{r}
dim(speBreast)
```

Which are the names of the assays?

```{r}
assayNames(speBreast)
```

Which gene ID is used in the assay?

```{r}
speBreast@rowRanges
```

What other type of additional information can be retrieved about the genes?

```{r}
head(rowData(speBreast))
```

What other type of additional information can be retrieved about the spots?

```{r}
colData(speBreast)
```

Which is the max and the min of the spatial coordinates?

```{r}
head(spatialCoords(speBreast))
coordinates <- spatialCoords(speBreast)
c(max(coordinates),min(coordinates))
range(coordinates)
```

## Visualize the data

Plotting the spatial coordinates and annotations

```{r}
plotCoords(speBreast, point_size = 5)
plotCoords(speBreast, point_size = 5, annotate = 'annotation')
```

Highlighting one specific spot

```{r}
coords <- as.data.frame(coordinates)
min_y_coord <- coords$pxl_row_in_fullres == min(coords$pxl_row_in_fullres)
min_x_coords <- coords$pxl_col_in_fullres == min(coords$pxl_col_in_fullres[min_y_coord])

top_left <- rownames(coords)[which(min_x_coords & min_y_coord)]
colData(speBreast)[, 'Top_Left'] <- as.character(colnames(speBreast) == top_left)

plotCoords(speBreast, annotate = "Top_Left", point_size = 5, pal = c('grey','red'))
```

Plotting the expression values for the VAMP7 gene. Highlight which are the sports with the max value of VAMP7 expression.

```{r}
vamp7 <- rownames(speBreast)[rowData(speBreast)$symbol == 'VAMP7'] 
plotCoords(speBreast, annotate = vamp7, point_size = 5) + ggtitle("VAMP7")

#Maximum expression

colData(speBreast)[, "maxVAMP7"] <- as.character(assay(speBreast)[vamp7,] == max(assay(speBreast)[vamp7,]))
plotCoords(speBreast, annotate = "maxVAMP7", point_size = 5, pal = c("grey","red"))
```

## Quality Control

Violin plot of the QC metrics and scatterplot of QC metrics together

```{r}
#First, we generate the GC features
#We add in metadata the QC parameter calculated by the method

speBreast <- quickRnaQc.se(speBreast, subsets = list())
head(colData(speBreast))

p1 <- plotObsQC(speBreast, 
    plot_type="scatter", 
    x_metric="detected", 
    y_metric="sum",
    y_threshold=600) + 
    ggtitle("Library size vs. cells per spot")
p1

```

We plot the QC

```{r}
plotObsQC(speBreast, plot_type = 'violin', x_metric = 'sum') + 
    xlab("Library size")
plotObsQC(speBreast, plot_type = 'violin', x_metric = 'detected')  + 
    xlab("Genes per spot")
```


```{r}
# select QC thresholds for library size, 
# detected features & mito. proportion
speBreast$qc_lib_size <- speBreast$sum < 600
speBreast$qc_detected <- speBreast$detected < 400

# tabulate number of cells kept/flagged by each
qc <- grep("^qc", names(colData(speBreast)))
sapply(colData(speBreast)[qc], table)

# check spatial pattern of discarded spots
p1 <- plotObsQC(speBreast, 
    plot_type="spot", annotate="qc_lib_size") + 
    ggtitle("Library size (< 600 UMI)")

p2 <- plotObsQC(speBreast, 
    plot_type="spot", annotate="qc_detected") + 
    ggtitle("Detected genes (< 400 genes)")

p1
p2
```

## Normalization

A simple and fast approach for normalization is 'library size normalization', which consists of calculating log-transformed nomralized counts ('log counts') using library size factors.
This method is simple, fast and generally provides a good baseline.

 - Plot the histogram of the size factors and the expression of the normalized VAMP7 gene expression.
 
```{r}
# calculate logcounts using library size factors
spe <- normalizeRnaCounts.se(speBreast)

summary(sizeFactors(spe))
```

```{r}
hist(sizeFactors(spe), breaks = 50, main = "Histogram of size factors")
```

```{r}
#assayNames(spe)

plotCoords(speBreast, annotate = vamp7, point_size = 5) + ggtitle("VAMP7")
plotCoords(spe, annotate = vamp7, assay_name='logcounts', point_size = 5) + ggtitle("VAMP7 Normalized")
```

## Feature selection
Feature selection methods can identify highly variable genes (HVGs) and spatially variable genes (SVGs)
### HVGs
Compute the fit mean-variance relationship. and visualize it
```{r}
# fit mean-variance relationship and select top HVGs
spe <- chooseRnaHvgs.se(
    spe, 
    top = ceiling(0.1 * nrow(spe)),
    more.var.args = list(use.min.width = TRUE))

# plot
rd <- rowData(spe)
plot(rd$means, rd$variances, 
    xlab = "mean (logexpr)", ylab = "variance (logexpr)")
o <- order(rd$means)
lines(rd$means[o], rd$fitted[o], col = "dodgerblue")
```


Select the top 10% of the HVGs. How many are there?
```{r}
# select top HVGs
sel <- rownames(spe)[rd$hvg]
# number of HVGs selected
length(sel)
MVG <- rowData(spe)$symbol[which.max(rd$variances)]
MVG
SPP1 <- rownames(speBreast)[rowData(speBreast)$symbol == 'SPP1'] 
```


Plot the normalized expression values of the most variable gene
```{r}
plotCoords(spe, annotate =SPP1 , assay_name='logcounts', point_size = 5) + ggtitle("SPP1")
```
